lines: Casey Morgan
+1 (555) 010-7731 | casey.morgan@example.com | example.com/portfolio/cmorgan
EDUCATION
Lakeshore University | B.A. in Cognitive Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2015 - May 2019
EXPERIENCE
Harborview Surf School | Surf Instructor | Metro City, USA | Aug 2025 - Present
- Taught weekend group lessons to beginners aged 8 to 60, keeping each class to one instructor for every six students.
- Ran the rental desk's morning equipment checks and logged board and wetsuit repairs for the shop owner.
Northwind Health | UX Research Associate | Metro City, USA | Jul 2019 - Feb 2022
- Raised the patient app's Net Promoter Score from 6.1 to 8.4, calculated as the average 0-10 recommendation rating across 2,000 monthly survey responses.
- Interviewed 40 patients about appointment reminders; the findings led to a two-way text reminder that cut missed appointments from 14% to 9%.
- Writes the screener and consent templates for all patient studies, cutting study setup time from two weeks to three days.
- Tested the telehealth waiting-room screens with 16 older patients; the revised layout cut support calls about joining a video visit by 30%.
Pinegrove Financial | Senior UX Researcher | Metro City, USA | Mar 2022 - Jun 2025
- Led research on the mobile onboarding flow, testing three prototypes with 24 new customers; the shipped design raised completed sign-ups from 41% to 58% in the quarter after launch.
- Improved dispute-form completion by 40% by splitting the form into three short steps with saved progress.
- Ran 18 moderated usability sessions a quarter from a recruiting panel of 400 customers, so every major release was tested with real account holders before launch.

- Synthesizing 60 interviews, 400 survey responses and 18 months of support tickets through affinity mapping, journey mapping and a tagged clip library, cut repeat support calls about statements by 23%.
- Raised the onboarding flow's System Usability Scale score from 68 to 104 across two rounds of moderated testing with 20 customers.
- Trained 12 product managers to run their own unmoderated tests with a shared script template, which doubled the number of tests run each quarter.
PROJECTS
Accessible Transit Map | Independent Project | Figma | Sep 2024 - Present
- Redesigned a city transit map for screen-reader and low-vision riders, and tested it with 12 participants on timed route-finding tasks.
- Measured the redesign with timed tasks: median route-finding time fell from 95 to 62 seconds and errors from 11 to 3 across the 12 sessions.
- Raised task success by 20% across 12 participants, from 65% to 85%, with audio landmarks and high-contrast line colors.
Community Clinic Booking Redesign | Volunteer, Team of 3 | Figma | Mar 2023 - Aug 2023
- Conducted user interviews and created wireframes for a free clinic's online booking flow.
- Ten clinic patients were recruited and two rounds of hallway testing were run, and the six issues that stopped first-time users were fixed.
- Wrote the clinic's volunteer handbook for maintaining the booking pages, which two later volunteer teams used to add Spanish-language booking.
SKILLS
Tools: Figma, screen-reader testing (VoiceOver, NVDA)
Methods: moderated and unmoderated usability testing, interviews, surveys, A/B testing

items.says: The contact details look like placeholders.
items.because: The phone number, email, and portfolio URL should be real and working.

items.says: Make sure the portfolio demonstrates the research and outcomes claimed.
Move Education below Experience.
items.because: The more relevant UX research work should appear first.

items.says: Put the experience roles in reverse chronological order.
items.because: Northwind appears before the more recent Pinegrove role.

items.says: Keep date and location formatting consistent across role headers.
Indicate whether the surf role is part-time.
items.because: That would help readers understand its overlap with the UX search or projects.

items.says: Add an outcome or specific responsibility, or shorten the teaching bullet.
items.because: The age range and ratio establish scope but not what you accomplished.

items.says: Explain the effect of the equipment checks or repair logs, if measurable.
items.because: Without that, the bullet is less relevant than the research experience.

items.says: An average 0–10 recommendation rating is not a Net Promoter Score.
Establish how the rating change was attributable to your work.
items.because: The monthly response count alone does not do that.

items.says: Clarify whether the missed-appointment rates are comparable before and after launch.
Identify the period over which missed appointments were measured.
Change “Writes” to past tense.
Clarify your contribution to the setup-time reduction.
items.because: Other process changes may have been involved.

items.says: Specify the period or basis for the 30% support-call comparison.
Verify that 41% and 58% use the same definition of “completed sign-up.”
Verify that the quarter-after-launch comparison is fair.
Clarify whether 40% is a relative or percentage-point increase.
Distinguish your research contribution from the team's design changes.
Replace the claim that every major release was tested if you cannot substantiate it.
Fix the opening verb.
items.because: The bullet is not grammatically complete.

items.says: Separate the research synthesis from the subsequent product or service change.
items.because: It is unclear what actually reduced calls.

items.says: A System Usability Scale score of 104 is impossible.
Check that both testing rounds were scored using the same method.
Specify the before-and-after quarterly test counts, if available.
items.because: That would make “doubled” easier to assess.

items.says: Clarify whether participants included screen-reader users and low-vision riders.
State what was tested, not just what was redesigned.
Clarify whether the time and error figures are per task, per participant, or totals across sessions.
Use comparable denominators for both versions.
Going from 65% to 85% is 20 percentage points, not a 20% increase.
Explain the denominator for the task-success percentages.
items.because: They do not map cleanly to 12 people unless each completed multiple tasks.

items.says: Consider combining this evidence with the preceding measurement bullet.
Add a research finding or design decision from the interviews.
Clarify who fixed the six issues.
Clarify whether a second round confirmed the issues were resolved.
Simplify the passive construction.
Consider whether other tools central to the projects belong here.
Keep A/B testing only if you can point to meaningful A/B-test work.
items.because: The experience bullets currently do not show such work.
